description: Read a pulse program (OpenPulse calibrations: ports, frames, waveforms, play, delay, shift_phase, set_phase, shift_frequency, set_frequency, captures and barriers) into its schedule on frames: every instruction at its sample, each waveform's samples (gaussian, drag, gaussian_square, constant, sech, sine, or explicit), each gate call with the samples its calibration spans, and the digests a pulse run's receipt binds (the program, its calibrations, the schedule). Durations are whole samples of dt (pulse.dt_ns, default 0.5 ns) or refused. A construct the reader does not take is refused with a Q code and its line. Sealed with the service's key. To run it, give the program to run_quantum_circuit with method "pulse".

pulse.description: A pulse run's options (method "pulse"): the sample period, the levels kept, the tolerance on the stated error, the steps a sample is divided into, each qubit's parameters, static couplings, and ports beyond the names d0, m0, a0.

levels.description: Levels kept per qubit (default 2; 3 shows leakage).

ports.description: Ports by name: what each is for and the qubit it reaches.

rabi_mhz.description: Its Rabi frequency at full amplitude, MHz.

qubits.description: Each qubit's parameters by its index, over the target's and the defaults.

substeps.description: Steps per sample (default: chosen so each step times the generator's norm is at most 0.5).

tolerance.description: The most the stated error may be (default 1e-6): a run whose bound and rounding estimate pass it is refused, naming the steps that would meet it.

qasm.description: A pulse program: OpenQASM 3 with `defcalgrammar "openpulse";`, `cal` blocks declaring ports (d0 drives qubit 0, m0 is its measurement port, a0 its acquisition port), frames (newframe(port, frequency Hz, phase)) and waveforms, a `defcal` for every gate it calls on physical qubits ($0), and the calls.

name: pulse_schedule

anyOf.description: A pulse answer as every host gives it (engine::pulse: pulse_schedule and pulse_check on both servers, wai-quantum pulse, POST /v1/pulse/*, the Studio): the request, and the result sealed in a job's form. A pulse program's schedule on frames, or a pulse job checked by running it again. A pulse run itself is a job (method pulse) and follows job-result.v1.json. A result names the engine that made it and this schema (engine and schema). docs/pulse.md explains each.

A pulse program's schedule (pulse_schedule, wai-quantum pulse schedule, POST /v1/pulse/schedule): its frames and ports, every instruction at its sample, each waveform's samples, the gate calls, the reader's notes, and the digests a run binds.

calibration.description: What a pulse run's receipt binds of the program: the BLAKE3 of the control program's text, of its calibrations as written (every cal, defcal and defcalgrammar, joined by newlines), and of the schedule's JSON; a run adds the device's and the target snapshot's.

duration.description: The latest time of any frame, samples.

engine.description: The engine that made the result: the wai-quantum crate's name and version.

carrier.description: The carrier's phase at the play's first sample, cycles in [0, 1).

receipt.description: A result's receipt: an Ed25519 signature, by the key it names, over digest = BLAKE3("wai:quantum-service-receipt\x02" ‖ len ‖ request ‖ len ‖ result), each of request and result in its RFC 8785 canonical text (the result without its receipt member), each length 8 bytes big-endian. Whatever members the request and the result hold are sealed, the result's engine and schema among them. The first receipts (no canon member, $defs/first) signed serde_json's own text under the domain ending \x01; they still verify.

canon.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over.

digest.description: The digest signed, 32 bytes in hex.

key.description: The signing key, 32 bytes in hex.

samples_every.description: Each k-th sample is drawn, when the schedule holds more than the view writes out.
